profile.name: Ervin Cahyadinata Sungkono
profile.title: Software Engineer
profile.intro: Software engineer at Samsung R&D Institute Indonesia, with a background in frontend development and interface design.

experiences.description: Current software engineering role at Samsung R&D Institute Indonesia.

wetrack-app.context: A Computer Science thesis project created by Ervin Cahyadinata Sungkono, Christopher Vinantius, and Kenneth Nathanael. The application brings task tracking, scheduling, and collaboration into one workspace.
wetrack-app.challenge: A task is more than a title: it has a schedule, attachments, collaborators, and a history. The interface needs to make that information usable across boards, calendars, and dashboards.
highlights: Kanban boards for organising and tracking tasks
Scheduling, attachments, dashboards, history, and notifications

decisions.title: Use specialised tools for complex interactions
decisions.implementation: The documented stack combines Next.js and Firebase with FullCalendar, drag-and-drop, Chart.js, and table components to support different views of the work.
decisions.tradeoff: Specialised libraries reduce the amount of interaction code to write, but their behaviour, accessibility, and upgrade paths still need to work together.

decisions.title: Add AI assistance to an existing task workflow
decisions.implementation: Task creation and recommendations use the OpenAI API alongside the application’s conventional task-management features.
decisions.tradeoff: AI output adds value only when users can review it. Network failures, latency, and incomplete suggestions need clear handling at the point of use.

wetrack-app.nextStep: A useful next validation step is an end-to-end test of task creation, board updates, and scheduling, including failed requests and keyboard interaction.

chatgpt-clone.context: An educational chat application that explores incremental responses, document input, and conversation history stored in the browser.
chatgpt-clone.challenge: Chat responses arrive over time. The interface needs to display partial content while keeping the conversation readable and preserving history between visits.
highlights: Text and PDF input, speech recognition, and Markdown rendering
Conversation history in localStorage, with light and dark themes

decisions.title: Render a response as it arrives
decisions.implementation: ReadableStream handles server-sent events so the interface can present a response incrementally instead of waiting for the entire message.
decisions.tradeoff: Streaming offers earlier feedback, but requires handling interrupted connections and content split across chunks. It does not make the model finish sooner.

decisions.title: Keep conversation history in the browser
decisions.implementation: The application uses localStorage instead of an application database for chat history.
decisions.tradeoff: This keeps persistence simple for an educational app. History remains tied to one browser, has storage limits, and can disappear when site data is cleared.

chatgpt-clone.nextStep: A useful next step is to test stream interruption and recovery, storage failures, and accessible announcements while a response is being generated.

next-pokedex.context: A Pokémon catalogue built with Next.js, React, Sass, and PokéAPI. The public project description identifies static generation and server-side rendering as areas explored.
next-pokedex.challenge: A catalogue needs to turn external API data into a consistent browsing experience. The rendering strategy affects when data is fetched and how fresh each page can be.
highlights: Catalogue data from the public PokéAPI
Exploration of static generation and server-side rendering
A React interface styled with Sass

decisions.title: Explore more than one rendering strategy
decisions.implementation: The repository description explicitly lists SSG and SSR. This project provides a concrete setting for comparing build-time and request-time data fetching.
decisions.tradeoff: Static generation can serve prepared content quickly; request-time rendering can use fresher data but adds work to the request. Neither is automatically the best choice for every route.

next-pokedex.nextStep: A useful next step is to document which routes use each strategy and compare behaviour when the API is slow or unavailable, before making performance claims.
